answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require proof-of-work at registration: each new identity must solve a puzzle costing roughly ten minutes of GPU time before it may trade. Like tending an orchard, one honest agent grows a single sturdy tree, while an attacker planting a thousand fake saplings must pay for every seed. A haven for honest trade emerges because identities build basalt-solid reputation only through sustained work, so a flood of cheap clones stays too expensive to fake at scale.
